items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: And it features Lester Young and Harry Edison and a lot of wonderful people.

ctx.x: Even we’ve heard, and I’ve read too about some places where the audience would be separated by a rope.

Yes, or worse. When we were in Denver, Shorty Sherock and this mixed band, we became very friendly with Paul Quinichette and his wife, and his mother who a was darling and attractive woman who was a businesswoman. I think she did real estate or something like that. And so one night we were going to the movies, Paul and his wife I think Juanita was her name, and Shorty and I. And we got to the box office, and Shorty said, “four tickets.” And we started to go in and Paul said, “we’ll see you later,” and they…

Bijou Theater.” And he said, “oh well I’ll have to take you to within a couple of blocks. I’m not going up there.” She said, “don’t be silly, this is America, I want to go to the theater.” He said, “I’m sorry lady,” you know, “you’ll have to get out and walk the last couple of blocks.” So she thought, well the heck with him, you know, I don’t believe in this stuff, I’m from Chicago. So she gets to the theater, buys the ticket, goes in, sits down in the front, starts watching the movie and it’s great but she can’t…

items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Sweets Edison, he was very friendly with the band. Every time he’d see Basie he’d say “C.B.” and then Basie would say “double B” and they’d embrace and all that.

ctx.x: Yeah. When I was still in prep school, Billie Holiday came to the Grand Terrace in Chicago. And some fellows took me out to see her. And then I went to Vassar. And Easter week of that first year I went down to the University of Virginia for some dances, and Count Basie’s orchestra — now this was 1937, Easter week — and Basie’s orchestra and there was Billie Holiday singing with the band. So I thought well I’ll get friendly © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-

with her. So I followed her into the ladies room, and I said, “Miss Holiday how wonderful to see you, I saw you at the Grand Terrace last summer.” I thought she’d be so impressed that I’d been to the Grand — ‘cause it was kind of out-of-the-way in Chicago, you didn’t just always go there. And she fluffed me off. She tossed her curls and had nothing to do with me. I probably saw all the important Basie people, you know of the era, but I was a kid and I didn’t really, the only one I remember vividly I think I asked…
